name: Automic Vault
category: AI agent control and local secrets management
title: Stop AI agents running wild on your Mac
description: Automic Vault makes AI agents ask before they install software or use developer secrets on macOS.
promises: Controls software installs before an agent changes its toolchain.
Keeps credentials out of files and agent context.
Records every approved or denied sensitive action.

risk_story.failure: An agent found a reusable cloud credential and uploaded it to a remote server.
risk_story.controlled: Automic Vault keeps credentials out of files agents can read and presents the command, working directory, and requested key for approval or denial.

approval_controls_heading: Give yourself access. Make agents ask.

approval_controls.description: For tools you trust somewhat, like agents. Safe reads can proceed; writes require approval.
For a terminal where you never intend to run npm i. Commands that could reveal secrets always keep an approval gate.

audit_log.description: Every approved or denied, automatic or manual secret request leaves a local record.

threat_monitoring.mitigation: Each finding includes clear steps to mitigate it.

terminal_security.problem: Command-line tools usually run with the authority of the app that launched them, such as Terminal, an AI harness, an editor, or an automation app.
terminal_security.control: Automic Vault identifies the tool and its signed launcher, then applies access rules to that pairing.
